recent_posts.title: Say What You See: Building Multimodal Content Signals at Scale
recent_posts.summary: Agoda built a Multimodal Content System that bridges the gap between hotel images and guest reviews by introducing a shared topic taxonomy. The system clusters images and reviews under common topics (e.g., Breakfast, Pool, Room Quality), enabling a unified view with relevant images, review snippets, and sentiment scores. At scale, it processes 450M+ images and millions of multilingual reviews daily using PySpark jobs orchestrated via Kubeflow, with results served from Couchbase. Three core pipelines handle image curation, review snippet extraction, and sentiment aggregation per topic. A/B tests showed doubled click rates on multimodal highlights on mobile and consistently positive engagement metrics across platforms. The next step is consolidating all content signals through LLMs into a single unified model.

recent_posts.title: From Implementers to Solution Architects
recent_posts.summary: As AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor accelerate code generation, the real bottleneck in software development has shifted from implementation to specification and verification. Individual productivity gains aren't translating to project velocity because vague specs and review overload become the new constraints. The post introduces a 'Grey Box' model—treating AI as a capable but imperfect collaborator requiring clear instructions and evidence-based validation. Engineers must evolve from implementers to solution architects: writing precise, testable specifications upfront, using AI to refine those specs, and shifting code review from line-by-line inspection to verifying that tests and automated checks prove the implementation meets the spec. Practical steps include investing in spec quality, designing testable integration points, and developing specification evaluation as a core engineering skill.

recent_posts.title: APIAgent converts any API to MCP using SQL post processing with DuckDB
recent_posts.summary: APIAgent is an open-source universal MCP server that connects AI assistants to any GraphQL or REST API without custom integration code. It automatically introspects API schemas, translates natural language questions into queries, and uses DuckDB for SQL-based post-processing to handle large result sets that exceed LLM context limits. The tool supports read-only operations by default, includes observability via OpenTelemetry, and can extract reusable query patterns (recipes) to optimize repeated questions. A single deployment can serve multiple APIs simultaneously by using per-request configuration headers.

recent_posts.title: How Agoda Enhanced the Uptime and Consistency of Financial Metrics
recent_posts.summary: Agoda consolidated multiple financial data pipelines into a single centralized system called FINUDP to address data inconsistencies, quality issues, and reliability concerns. The unified pipeline processes millions of daily financial data points using Apache Spark, achieving 95.6% uptime with a goal of 99.5%. Key improvements include hourly data updates, automated quality checks using tools like Quilliup and GoFresh, shadow testing, staging environments, and data contracts with upstream teams. The centralization reduced pipeline runtime from five hours to 30 minutes while establishing a single source of truth for financial metrics across the organization.

recent_posts.title: Agoda Dev Day 2025: Celebrating Collaboration in our Tech Team
recent_posts.summary: Agoda hosted their internal Dev Day 2025 in Bangkok, bringing together their tech team for knowledge sharing and collaboration. The event featured a tech leadership keynote, a speed coding competition, lightning talks on AI agents, security threats in chatbots, and infrastructure topics, a career growth panel discussion, and a debate on testing strategies comparing fakes versus mocks for integration testing.

recent_posts.title: Migrating from Enzyme to Playwright: How We Modernized Frontend Testing at Agoda
recent_posts.summary: Agoda migrated their frontend testing from Enzyme to Playwright to address limitations in cross-browser support, asynchronous interactions, and visual regression detection. The migration involved switching from Webpack to Vite for faster development, implementing screenshot-based testing to reduce test count by 6-7×, and integrating accessibility and analytics checks into automated workflows. Key improvements include cross-browser and RTL/LTR layout testing, Docker-based baseline standardization for consistent visual testing, and performance optimizations through caching and component consolidation. While Playwright requires more setup and resources per test, it provides broader coverage, better stability through actionability checks, and catches visual regressions that code assertions miss.

recent_posts.title: Migrating Agoda's feature store from Scala to Rust for 5x traffic growth
recent_posts.summary: Agoda migrated their Feature Store Serving component from Scala to Rust to address latency issues and scaling bottlenecks. Despite having no prior Rust experience, the team completed a proof of concept in one week using AI tools and the Rust compiler. After migration, they achieved 84% cost reduction while handling 5x more traffic, with CPU usage at 40% and memory at 15% of previous Scala levels. Shadow testing validated correctness before production deployment. The migration demonstrates how Rust's performance characteristics and modern tooling can enable teams to overcome JVM limitations in high-throughput, latency-sensitive systems.

recent_posts.title: Interns in Action: Building Tools to Reduce Bugs at Agoda
recent_posts.summary: Two engineering interns at Agoda developed a system to analyze historical bug data and identify patterns that could help prevent future bugs. They built an ETL pipeline using PySpark on Kubeflow to collect code complexity and coverage metrics, created a Superset dashboard for visualization, and used LLMs to accurately identify bug-causing files with 90% accuracy. While code metrics alone couldn't reliably predict bugs, their work led to a successful integration with Agoda's AI-assisted code review tool, providing developers with historical bug context during reviews. The feature is now deployed across 400 projects and receives 78% positive feedback.

recent_posts.title: A Retrospective: Agoda’s GenAI Journey Thus Far
recent_posts.summary: Agoda shares their two-year journey implementing generative AI across their organization, starting with a company-wide hackathon in February 2023. The travel company now has over 200 GenAI applications and services, with 73% of employees using AI productivity tools and 45% of internal tech support tickets handled by AI. Key success factors included building centralized infrastructure (GenAI Proxy), fostering grassroots adoption through community channels, creating internal chat platforms, and focusing on practical use cases that deliver measurable value. The approach emphasized learning through internal tools before scaling to customer-facing features.
